deviations.what: ReviewListView.filterset_fields is pinned to [] rather than left at FairDMListView's default.
deviations.why: FairDMListView auto-generates a django-filter FilterSet from every model field when none is configured; django-filter has no mapping for Review's PartialDateField start_date/end_date and raises AssertionError the first time the page is requested. Filtering is not in US-1's scope (not in spec.md or plan.md's access table), so an empty field list disables the auto-generation without adding a feature nobody asked for.

deviations.what: T014's route registration landed inside T011's commit; T013 was implemented after T014 rather than before, reversing two adjacent entries in tasks.md's listed order (T011, T012, T013, T014).
deviations.why: This repo's established view-test convention (tests/test_ghfdb/test_views.py) is client.get(reverse(...)), which needs the route to already exist, and AssessmentMenuItem.check() resolves its view_name through flex_menu's own reverse() call, which needs the same thing. T013's acceptance test would otherwise pass for the wrong reason (invisible because the URL fails to resolve, not because the role check refused it). Every task still lands as its own commit with its own tests, in its own task ID.

deviations.what: The 'served' access tests (a Data Assessor/Data Curator being granted entry) use RequestFactory and stop at the unrendered TemplateResponse (T011) or call AssessmentMenuItem.check() directly (T013), rather than asserting against a fully rendered page. T012's item-template test renders that one template directly via render_to_string rather than through the full list page.
deviations.why: Discovered mid-story: any authenticated request that reaches this project's shared page chrome (the sidebar's AppMenu render) raises KeyError('request'). It reproduces identically, with no review/ code involved, on the pre-existing /datasets/ page for any logged-in user. This is upstream of project/review/, sitewide, and not something this story's files can fix. The refusal paths (PermissionDenied, the anonymous redirect) are unaffected since both short-circuit before any template renders, so those still use the ordinary test client. See concerns.

deviations.what: project/review/apps.py gained a ready() hook that imports review.menus explicitly; review/menus.py imports AppMenu from fairdm.menus rather than mvp.menus.
deviations.why: Nothing autodiscovers a 'menus' module the way Django admin autodiscovers admin.py, so without an explicit import assessment_entry would never actually register on a running site, even though importing the module directly for a test makes the tests pass regardless - confirmed the gap by checking the app registry (root.get('AppMenu')) after a bare django.setup(), with no test importing review.menus itself. fairdm.menus.AppMenu is the identical object mvp.menus.AppMenu is (project/ghfdb/menus.py already imports it this way) but mvp is only a transitive dependency of this project's pyproject.toml, and deptry flags a direct import of it as DEP003.

concerns: Sitewide defect, not fixed here (out of project/review/'s scope): any authenticated request to a page using the shared sidebar chrome (mvp's cotton/app/sidebar/index.html, {% render_menu %} for AppMenu) raises KeyError('request') during template rendering. Reproduces on the pre-existing /datasets/ page (fairdm.core.dataset.views.DatasetListView) for any logged-in user; anonymous requests to the same page render fine. Root-caused as far as instrumenting flex_menu.templatetags.flex_menu.process_menu shows: the first render_menu call for a page carries a real RequestContext, every subsequent call for the same page (the sidebar and the mobile dock both call it) carries a plain Context with no request bound - consistent with django_cotton re-rendering a component via render_to_string() without forwarding the request on a repeat pass. This blocks every authenticated visitor from viewing any portal list page right now, including the ones this story adds, and needs its own investigation (D16 has the full reproduction).

project/ghfdb/menus.py has the same 'never actually imported' gap review/menus.py had before D17's fix: its one navigation entry (GHFDB Map Viewer) is not wired through any ready() hook or autodiscovery and does not currently register into AppMenu on a running site, despite existing as source. Left alone as outside project/review/'s scope; worth its own one-line fix analogous to D17's.
